what_this_is: The Workshop rows for the tools in tools/export-documents-to-files: what each tool does, what it takes and gives back, and how it runs.

payload.label: Save a document as a Word file, a PDF, Markdown or plain text (runs on your computer)
payload.job: Turn a document written as a tree of text blocks into a Word (docx) file, a PDF, a Markdown file or a plain text file, with headings, paragraphs and tables kept in order
payload.description: Takes a job file and a rules file. The job holds the title, the tree (each node has props with its text, a heading level if it is one, and children; a node with children that all hold two or more short texts is read as a table row, two or more such rows as a table) and a descriptor: format_id, destination_dir (a full path) and file_stem (a plain name, no folder). The rules file is a JSON list of rows of kind structured-file-projection-rules; each names which props carry text, where a heading level is, and per format how the body is built (Markdown and text by templates, Word by heading, body and table styles, PDF by a TrueType font file name and heading sizes). A starter rules file is in read-data/starter-projection-rules.json. Word is written with the standard library only. PDF needs the reportlab library and the named font; an unreadable font or a character the font cannot draw stops the export with a message, never a substituted character. The file is read back and compared to what was meant before the result is printed. Add --project-only to see the sections the tree would give without writing a file.

job.description: Path of the JSON job file: title, tree, descriptor

rules.description: Path of the JSON rules file (a list of structured-file-projection-rules rows)

get_it: for PDF only: python3 with the reportlab library
invoke.say: This runs on the person's own computer, from the root of the Workshop checkout. Write the job file from the document the person means and, unless they gave rules, start from read-data/starter-projection-rules.json. Run `run`; the last line is the JSON result with the path of the new file. A message with an error key says what to fix (a format the rules do not have, a destination that is not a full path, a font or a character the PDF cannot use). Tell the person where the file is. If you cannot run commands, give them these steps.

provenance.source: ported from bitfield-packages packages/structured-file-output (render-structured-file-export); the content hash is no longer printed, hash the file with tools/content-identity

payload.label: Write a web page from one record and a description of how to publish it (runs on your computer)
payload.job: Turn one record and a publication descriptor into a finished web page: its words, its address, its search and sharing tags, its structured data and a proof of what it was made from
payload.description: Takes an envelope file: publication_descriptor, source_record, optional materialized_values and correlation_id. The descriptor says which record fields become the title, description, language and page sections (heading, paragraph, prose, list, quote, code, image, group; any other operation still shows its text), where the page will live (scheme, domain and path pieces, each a literal or a value read from the record), the colours and font (tokens), extra sharing tags, and a list of structured-data nodes whose values are read from the record, with empty values dropped. Words from the record are escaped; a prose section is written as given, so its owner must have made it safe. The new page is written to the output path. The answer gives the address, tags, byte count and a proof naming the descriptor, record and revision it came from.

envelope.description: Path of the JSON envelope file

output.description: Path of the HTML file to write

invoke.say: This runs on the person's own computer, from the root of the Workshop checkout. Write the envelope from the record the person means and the way they want it published, run `run`, and read the last JSON line. This only writes the file; putting it on a site is a separate step the person must ask for. Tell them the address it was written for and where the file is. If you cannot run commands, give them these steps.

provenance.source: ported from bitfield-packages packages/public-document-renderer (render-public-document, RecordPublicationProjection); the default typeface is now the system one

payload.label: Export a Markdown book to Word through its writing checks, and verify the Word file and its PDF against the source (runs on your computer)
payload.job: export a markdown manuscript to word and verify it against its source
payload.description: Reads the book's settings row (record:setting:export-documents-to-files~piece~<book_id>, list:settings): its manuscript, role (current_prose, comparison or historical_reference), the BLAKE3 its bytes must have, a retained Word template and output folder, and for current prose the checks branch, writing profile, reviews and captured book-voice runs in its evidence folder. For current prose it first runs the book's checks branch of list:checks (tools/check-against-a-persons-rules-and-verdicts, branch mode) on the exact bytes and stops when they do not pass; then the writing gate checks the writing profile and review evidence (tools/pin-files-by-content), and the captured voice-classifier run and its qualification benchmark (tools/train-and-evaluate-a-writing-voice-classifier). Only then is the Word file built from the template (title, a clickable contents list with page fields, heading bookmarks, native tables, lists, quotes, footer page numbers), read back and compared to the source. verify_book_against_its_source.py checks the Word file and a rendered PDF against the source (outline, contents links, page map, body text with two PDF readers) and can repair confirmed ligature mappings. Passing proves coverage and regression checks only, never author approval.

book_id.description: The piece id of the book's settings row

settings_record.description: The settings row id, when it is not record:setting:export-documents-to-files~piece~<book_id>

manuscript.description: Path of the Markdown manuscript (else the settings' manuscript)

template.description: Path of the retained Word template (else the settings' template)

output.description: Path of the Word file to write (else <output_folder>/<book_id>.docx)

page_map.description: Path of the BookHeadingN to page JSON the verifier wrote, for the second pass

answers.description: Answers to the checks branch's reading questions, by question id

get_it: python3 with python-docx; pypdf and pypdfium2 for the PDF verifier; LibreOffice to render the PDF
needs: the person's records door (stdio client config)
invoke.say: This runs on the person's own computer, from the root of the Workshop checkout, with their records door. Write the request ({ book_id }, plus a manuscript, template or output when they differ from the book's settings row) to a file and run `run`; the last line is { result }. status exported names the Word file; blocked says why (no settings row, changed source bytes, the book's checks failed or have unanswered reading questions, the writing profile or review evidence, the voice-classifier evidence). When the checks ask reading questions, answer them and send `answers`. Then render the Word file to PDF (soffice --headless --convert-to pdf) and run `python3 tools/export-documents-to-files/do-work/verify_book_against_its_source.py --source MD --docx DOCX --raw-pdf PDF --page-map-out MAP --report REPORT`; rebuild with page_map set to MAP, render and verify again. Tell the person what passed and every unresolved difference. Never say the book is approved: these are coverage checks. If you cannot run commands, give them these steps.

provenance.source: moved from Trillion-X/source-repo-a tools/private-book-reader (private_book_reader.py, writing_gate.py, verify_pdf_source.py) at 5a9ba3988a4d; the .writing-policy.json beside the manuscript became the book's settings row, and the gate calls the Workshop's checks branch, pin-files-by-content and voice-classifier tools
